findings.summary: UserId brand in shared/ids.ts (`string & { __brand: 'UserId' }`) is structurally incompatible with the Zod-branded UserId in packages/contracts/src/auth.ts — same name, two parallel nominal types, downstream service code must cast across them
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one home for UserId: either (a) import UserId type from @medbridge/contracts and re-export from shared/ids.ts, dropping the local brand, OR (b) move the structural brand into contracts and have its Zod schema produce the same brand via z.string().uuid().transform(s => s as UserId). Decide before task-auth-service so the factory's user.id flow stays end-to-end-typed without `as`.

findings.summary: `export const env: Env = loadEnv();` runs at module-load time, so any transitive importer (logger.ts already does so on line 3) eagerly parses process.env on import — breaks pure-unit imports of logger without a real environment and couples test setup to env presence even when the test does not exercise env paths
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) drop the eager singleton and have call sites construct `loadEnv(process.env)` in main.ts/seed/main.ts and pass it down (matches the DI ethos already used for clock/hasher), OR (b) make `env` lazy via `let _env: Env | undefined; export const env = (): Env => (_env ??= loadEnv())` so importers that never touch env do not crash. The planner spec mentions a singleton but the fail-fast test only needs the `loadEnv(source)` factory, which is already exported.
